newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee still down by close, Sept bucks trend.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee still down by close, Sept bucks trend.

text.p: LIFFE robusta coffee futures stayed broadly lower by the close on Friday with the exception of September which bucked the trend to finish up as origin selling subsided.
September steadied up $5 late in the day with the contract moving back into the plus column at the close.
At the closing bell, it stood $4 higher on the day at $1,775. Other positions maintained a weaker trend but off their lows.
Traders said September was earlier slated for fund sell-stops at $1,755. "It went to a low of $1,745 but nothing happened," said one trader.
The bulk of the origin offers were from Africa, encouraged by the higher prices and firm French francs.
"The Africans were very happy with robusta at $1,200. Now prices are $500 above that," said one.
September and November again led actives, accounting for the bulk of the total's volume of 4,235 lots.
But the overall fundamental picture for the market remained weak with roasters generally well covered.

Easing concerns over Brazilian frost, USDA's restatement of a crop of 28 million bags for Brazil in 1997/98, and a build in New York exchange-certified stocks were the main underlying bearish factors.

"It's all coming to an end, slowly but surely," said one trader. The market had seen an unprecedented five-month rally that peaked in late May on aggressive fund and roaster buying, tight arabica supplies and frost fears in Brazil.

June and July are the frost-danger months in Brazil but so far there has been no crop-damaging freeze in the country's coffee-growing areas. Chances of a frost in the coming weeks are also slim, according to weathermen.
On the charts, coffee faces a major support at $1,695, the lower end of the June trading range. A break lower could see a swift move down to $1,600.
On the upside, a breakthrough at above $1,850 would pave the way for the market to regain a foothold at $2,040, a level last seen in May.
In its commentary on Friday, broker GNI said the odds of a frost from hereon were around 20:1, rising to 63:1 by the end of the month and 100:1 just five days after that.
"Clearly the frost premium should be eroding rapidly, and the current warm conditions are allowing this year's harvest to continue apace," it said.
